newsitem.title: UK: Sugar freight market sees fresh wave of inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Sugar freight market sees fresh wave of inquiry.

text.p: The sugar freight market was active with new orders on Tuesday, reflecting demand for the new European beet crop and continued interest in north Brazil's bumper cane harvest, shipbrokers said.
CSR dominated the day's new quoted business and issued three new orders for bulk sugar.
It quoted for 20,000 tonnes from Queensland to Japan for November 1/10 and 16,000 tonnes from the same origin to Prai for November 5/15.
CSR was also open for 10,500/11,000 tonnes from Wyndham to Kunsan for November 4/14, shipbrokers said.

Jean Lion also entered the market with some fresh inquiry for tonnage from Continent ports, quoting for 5/6,000 tonnes of bagged sugar to Algeria for prompt dates and a further 13/14,000 tonnes in bags to Damman or Jeddah for 14 days notice.
Genoc was in the market for 7/8,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio or Recife to Constanza for prompt dates.
Reported firmer business came from E D & F Man, which was said to be on subjects with a prompt 14/15,400-tonne bulk cargo from Maceio/Recife to Algeria or the Black Sea.

Shipbrokers said Mauritius Sugar Syndicate quickly fixed its recent inquiry for 15,200 tonnes of bulk sugar from Port Louis to Lisbon for October 23/26 but details of the rate achieved have yet to emerge.
